purpose: Explicit adjustments to the sourced codings in the group files. Each entry either corrects a figure the source itself shows to be something else, or widens a coding that an observer could reasonably score either way. Widening can only make the key more cautious; it never makes a sound key unsound.

Petinomys bullae have cobweb-type septa (more than four, not strictly honeycomb); the flying-squirrel follow-up scores these as yes, but an observer applying the narrower honeycomb definition would answer no, so both states. The three-state character bullar_septa records the distinction precisely.

Moore (1959, Table 1) reports per-specimen counts of 0, 1/2, 1 1/2, 2 1/2 and 4 pairs of transbullar septa (e.g. Ratufa 0 in 196 specimens and 1 in 2; Tamiasciurus 2-4; Microsciurus down to 0), which the coded states 1/2/3 cannot express; the character is therefore not used for any genus.
Ellerman (1940) keys Menetes under 'rostrum not extremely elongated', contradicting the 'yes' coding from another source; both states.
